model_annotations.Bulgarian:
**Figure 4:** This figure presents a line graph illustrating the mean absolute values of SDPA output before and after gating, plotted across 21 layers (labeled from 0 to 20 on the x-axis). The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 20, with tick marks and labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled “Mean Absolute Value,” uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1.4, with tick marks and labels at intervals of 0.2. The graph contains two lines: a dashed line representing “before gate” and a solid line representing “after gate.” Both lines remain nearly flat and close to each other across all layers, with values starting near 0.1 and increasing slightly to approximately 0.14 by layer 20. The legend indicates that the average values are 0.03 before gating and 0.03 after gating, suggesting minimal change.

**Figure 5:** This figure contains two side-by-side line graphs, both plotting the sparsity ratio of SDPA output across 21 layers (x-axis labeled “Layer,” linear scale from 0 to 20, with tick marks at intervals of 5). The left graph, titled “Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-2,” has a y-axis labeled “Sparsity Ratio” with a linear scale from 0 to 1.6, marked at intervals of 0.2. It displays three lines: a dashed line for “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03,” a dash-dotted line for “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.04,” and a solid line for “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33.” The dashed and dash-dotted lines remain near 0.03 and 0.04, respectively, across all layers, while the solid line starts near 0.03 and rises sharply to approximately 0.3 by layer 5, then continues to increase to about 1.6 by layer 20. The right graph, titled “Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-3,” has a y-axis with a linear scale from 0 to 0.8, marked at intervals of 0.2. It shows three lines: a dashed line for “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.126,” a dash-dotted line for “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.126,” and a solid line for “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.080.” The dashed and dash-dotted lines remain nearly flat at approximately 0.126 across all layers, while the solid line starts near 0.126 and decreases sharply to approximately 0.08 by layer 5, then remains relatively flat near 0.08 for the remaining layers. Both graphs include a legend specifying the average sparsity ratios for each condition.
model_annotations.Chinese:
Figure 4 displays the mean absolute values of SDPA output before and after gating across 20 layers, with the x-axis labeled "Layer" ranging from 0 to 20 in linear increments of 5. The y-axis, labeled "Mean Absolute Value," ranges from 0.0 to 1.4 in linear increments of 0.2. A single blue dashed line represents the mean absolute values, which remain relatively flat across layers, starting near 0.1 at Layer 0 and ending near 0.1 at Layer 20, with minor fluctuations; the caption notes that baseline and post-gating values are similar.

Figure 5 consists of two subplots showing the sparsity ratio of SDPA output values below a threshold, with the x-axis labeled "Layer" ranging from 0 to 20 in linear increments of 5 for both. The left subplot, titled "Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-2," has a y-axis labeled "Sparsity Ratio" ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 in linear increments of 0.2. It contains three lines: a green dashed line (sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03) that starts at approximately 0.03 at Layer 0 and decreases to near 0.0 at Layer 20; a blue dashed line (sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.04) that starts at approximately 0.04 and remains nearly flat; and an orange dashed line (sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33) that starts at approximately 0.33 and remains nearly flat. The right subplot, titled "Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-3," has a y-axis labeled "Sparsity Ratio" ranging from 0.0 to 0.8 in linear increments of 0.2. It contains three lines: a green dashed line (sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.02) that starts at approximately 0.02 and decreases to near 0.0 at Layer 20; a blue dashed line (sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.126) that starts at approximately 0.126 and remains nearly flat; and an orange dashed line (sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.088) that starts at approximately 0.088 and remains nearly flat. The caption indicates that sparsity measurements are obtained by multiplying the average gating score with pre-gating hidden states.
model_annotations.English:
Figure 4 displays the mean absolute values of SDPA output before and after gating, plotted against layer depth from 1 to 20. The x-axis, labeled "Layer," uses a linear scale with integer tick marks at intervals of 5 (0, 5, 10, 15, 20). The y-axis, labeled "Mean Absolute Value," ranges from 0 to 1.4 with a linear scale and tick marks at 0.1 intervals. Two lines are shown: a dashed gray line representing the mean absolute value before gating, which remains nearly constant around 0.1 across all layers; and a solid blue line representing the mean absolute value after gating, which also stays approximately constant at 0.1, indicating that the baseline and post-gating values are similar as noted in the caption.

Figure 5 presents two side-by-side line plots illustrating the sparsity ratio of SDPA output values below a given threshold, with the left plot using a threshold of 1e-2 and the right plot using 1e-3. Both plots share the same x-axis, labeled "Layer," which ranges from 0 to 20 with linear scaling and tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis in both plots is labeled "Sparsity Ratio" and ranges from 0 to 1.0 with linear scaling and tick marks at 0.2 intervals. In the left plot (threshold 1e-2), three lines are shown: a dashed gray line for "sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03," which starts at approximately 0.03 and remains nearly flat; a solid blue line for "sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.04," which starts at 0.04 and increases slightly to around 0.06 by layer 20; and a dotted green line for "sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33," which starts at 0.33 and rises sharply to nearly 1.0 by layer 20. In the right plot (threshold 1e-3), the dashed gray line for "sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.126" begins at approximately 0.126 and remains relatively flat; the solid blue line for "sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.126" starts at 0.126 and increases slightly to about 0.15 by layer 20; and the dotted green line for "sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.080" begins at 0.080 and rises sharply to nearly 1.0 by layer 20. The plots show that sparsity increases significantly after applying the average gate, especially with the lower threshold, while the sparsity after standard gating shows only minor changes.
model_annotations.German:
Figure 4 displays the mean absolute values of SDPA output before and after gating, plotted across 21 layers (from layer 1 to layer 20, with layer 21 implied by the x-axis range). The x-axis is labeled “Layer” and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 20, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis is labeled “Mean Absolute Value” and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1.4, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. Two lines are shown: a dashed line representing the mean absolute value before gating, which remains nearly constant at approximately 0.1 across all layers, and a solid line representing the mean absolute value after gating, which also remains nearly constant at approximately 0.1, showing minimal deviation from the pre-gating values. The two lines are visually indistinguishable, indicating that the gating operation does not significantly alter the mean absolute values of the SDPA output.

Figure 5 presents two side-by-side line plots illustrating the sparsity ratio of SDPA output values below a given threshold, across 21 layers. Both plots share the same x-axis, labeled “Layer,” with a linear scale from 0 to 20 and tick marks at intervals of 5. The left plot is titled “Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-2” and has a y-axis labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” ranging from 0 to 1.6 with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The right plot is titled “Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-3” and has a y-axis labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” ranging from 0 to 0.8 with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. In both plots, three lines are shown: a dashed line representing the sparsity ratio before gating, a dotted line representing the sparsity ratio after gating, and a dash-dotted line representing the sparsity ratio after average gating. In the left plot (threshold 1e-2), the dashed line starts at approximately 1.6 at layer 0 and decreases to about 0.2 at layer 20; the dotted line starts at approximately 0.4 at layer 0 and decreases to about 0.2 at layer 20; the dash-dotted line starts at approximately 0.33 at layer 0 and remains nearly constant at 0.33 across all layers. In the right plot (threshold 1e-3), the dashed line starts at approximately 0.8 at layer 0 and decreases to about 0.2 at layer 20; the dotted line starts at approximately 0.126 at layer 0 and decreases to about 0.08 at layer 20; the dash-dotted line starts at approximately 0.08 at layer 0 and remains nearly constant at 0.08 across all layers.
